title: He was nine years old when it was quenched.
html_source: Could this be a reference to the birth of Henry Wriothesley, 3rd Earl of Southampton, and the real identity, as thought by some, of the “Fair Youth” in Shakespeare’s sonnets? Wriothesley’s birth occurred nine years after Shakespeare’s. Of course, the sonnets being dedicated to “WH”, others believe the Fair Youth is the Willie Hughes, object of conjecture and sport in this chapter, or “WH” could also be William Herbert, 3rd Earl of Pembroke. Southamptonians argue Shakespeare was trying to disguise the real identity of the dedicatee, and so swapped the initials round from “HW”.
